entries.title: aikidō
entries.description: Defensive martial art developed by Ueshiba Morihei between 1925 and 1969.

entries.title: aikuchi
entries.description: Small Japanese dagger.

entries.title: Ainu
entries.description: Indigenous people of northern Japan, distinct from the Japanese in language and ancestry; their ancestors go back to the Jōmon culture. In Hokkaidō Prefecture’s 2023 survey, about 11,450 people identified as Ainu, and the number of their descendants is much higher. The Japanese long regarded them as barbarians and fought them for centuries, for example in Koshamain’s uprising of 1457 and Shakushain’s War of 1669–1672.

entries.title: aisha
entries.description: Principle of gojō goyoku that exploits a person’s compassion.

entries.title: Akechi Mitsuhide
entries.description: General of Oda Nobunaga who betrayed his lord. When Nobunaga was without his bodyguards, Akechi attacked and killed him. His troops burned Nobunaga’s castle to the ground.

entries.title: akindo
entries.description: A favorite ninja disguise from the shichi hō de.

entries.title: ametori no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of the birds in the rain
entries.description: Tactic that exploits the habit of guards to stay away from their posts, or keep watch half-heartedly, in rain or cold.

entries.title: amigasa
entries.description: Woven straw hat whose wide brim hides the face.

entries.title: ashi kō
entries.description: Foot claws that ninja used to climb walls. The counterpart for the hands is called shukō or tekagi.

entries.title: ashigaru
entries.description: The lower class of the samurai. In peacetime most of them worked as farmers in the fields. Their weapons and armor were lighter and cheaper.

entries.title: Ashikaga
entries.description: Clan descended from the Minamoto that held the office of shōgun in Japan during the Ashikaga period (1338–1573).

entries.title: ashinaka
entries.description: Straw sandals without a heel that cover only the front of the foot. The toes grip the ground directly and find a sure footing even on slippery terrain.

entries.title: atemi
entries.description: Punches and kicks against a person’s vital points and nerve centers to stun, paralyze, or kill.

entries.title: atemi waza
entries.description: Another term for striking the vital points and nerve centers.

entries.title: atemite
entries.translation: striking the body with the hand
entries.description: Another term for striking the vital points and nerve centers.

entries.title: bakemono jutsu
entries.description: The art of turning oneself into a ghost. Igasaki Dōjun is said to have used it to get into a fortress.

entries.title: bakufu
entries.description: Originally the shōgun’s field camp, later the seat of his military dictatorship. In English, the <q>shogunate</q>.

entries.title: bakuhatsu gama
entries.description: Ninja weapon made of a large sickle (kama) and a two-meter chain with explosives, poison, or blinding powder at its end.

entries.title: Bansenshūkai
entries.translation: ten thousand rivers flow into the sea
entries.description: Ten-part compendium of ninjutsu, written in 1676 by Fujibayashi Yasutake.

entries.title: banzai
entries.description: Japanese cry of joy and battle cry.

entries.title: bikenjutsu
entries.description: Sword fighting. With taijutsu and bōjutsu, one of the three pillars of ninpō.

entries.title: bisentō
entries.description: Japanese halberd with a broad blade.

entries.title: bisentōjutsu
entries.description: Fighting with the halberd (bisentō). One of the 18 fields of the ninja jūhakkei.

entries.title: Biwako
entries.description: The largest lake in Japan (about 670 km²), near Kyōto. It takes its name from its shape, which resembles a lute (biwa).

entries.title: bō
entries.description: Term for all Japanese staff weapons; in the narrower sense, the roku shaku bō.

entries.title: bō ken
entries.description: Practice sword made of heavy wood, also bokken or bokutō. A dangerous weapon in its own right.

entries.title: bō shuriken
entries.description: Long, dagger-like throwing weapons (shuriken), among them hairpins, nails, and chopsticks.

entries.title: bōbi no kamae
entries.description: Defensive stance (kamae).

entries.title: bōjutsu
entries.description: Staff fighting. With taijutsu and bikenjutsu, one of the three pillars of ninpō.

entries.title: bokken
entries.description: Also bō ken or bokutō.

entries.title: boku
entries.description: Also moku.

entries.title: bokutō
entries.description: Also bō ken or bokken.

entries.title: bōryaku
entries.description: Part of Japanese warfare (heihō) that includes, among other things, the battle formations.

entries.title: boshi ken
entries.description: Strike that hits the target with the tip of the thumb.

entries.title: bu
entries.description: Also mu.

entries.title: Buddha
entries.description: Term for a person who has broken the cycle of rebirth. Usually it means Siddhārtha Gautama, a prince from Kapilavastu and the founder of Buddhism. In Japanese, butsu.

entries.title: budō
entries.description: Umbrella term for all Japanese martial arts.

entries.title: budōka
entries.description: Someone who practices budō.

entries.title: bugei jūhappan
entries.description: The 18 categories of martial arts. A ninja needed a good grounding in them; on top of that came the 18 categories of secret techniques of the ninja jūhakkei.

entries.title: bugeisha
entries.description: Term for the warriors (samurai) who practiced the martial arts. Also bujin.

entries.title: bujin
entries.description: Also bugeisha.

entries.title: Bujinkan
entries.translation: the hall of the divine warrior
entries.description: Organization founded by Hatsumi Masaaki that unites nine old warrior and ninjutsu Ryū.

entries.title: bujutsu
entries.description: Term for all martial arts of the samurai.

entries.title: buke
entries.description: Term for the noble warrior families.

entries.title: bushi
entries.description: Term for the noble warriors of feudal Japan.

entries.title: bushidō
entries.description: Code of honor of the samurai that demanded self-discipline, self-sacrifice, and self-control.

entries.title: Chi ryaku no maki
entries.translation: scroll of the strategies of the earth
entries.description: Book on the strategies of the earth, part of a series with <cite>Ten ryaku no maki</cite> and <cite>Jin ryaku no maki</cite>.

entries.title: chigiriki
entries.description: Long staff with a chain and an iron weight at the end, a weapon that evolved from the flail.

entries.title: chikairi
entries.description: Strategies that ninja used in war to break through enemy lines.

entries.title: chiken-in
entries.translation: sign of the fist of wisdom
entries.description: Hand sign for retsu in kuji-in.

entries.title: chikujō jutsu
entries.translation: the art of building a castle
entries.description: Methods of field fortification.

entries.title: chikyū jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri. A captured ninja accepts the enemy lord’s offer of work and escapes at the first opportunity.

entries.title: chitsu mishi
entries.description: Inhabitants of enemy territory who work for a ninja.

entries.title: chōda
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: chōkyori kyōsō
entries.description: Running technique that ninja used to carry messages over long distances.

entries.title: chūnin
entries.description: Middle rank of the ninja, the link between a clan leader (jōnin) and the agents in the field (genin). Because the chūnin usually made contact with the client, their strengths lay in judging people and in disguise.

entries.title: daikongō-in
entries.description: Hand sign for pyō in kuji-in.

entries.title: daimyō
entries.description: The rising great landowners who fought for power in Japan during the Sengoku jidai.

entries.title: daisharin
entries.description: Ninja weapon made of an axle and two large wheels, rolled into the opponent’s legs.

entries.title: daishō
entries.description: The pair of swords of the samurai, katana and wakizashi.

entries.title: daitō
entries.description: Term for the samurai’s long sword, as opposed to the short sword.

entries.title: daken taijutsu
entries.translation: the art of striking the body with the fist
entries.description: Fighting techniques from taijutsu: kicks, punches, and blocks. They divide into koppō jutsu and koshi jutsu.

entries.title: dan
entries.description: Term for the master grades.

entries.title: Dao
entries.description: In Daoism, the highest reality and power of the universe, the ground of being and non-being. It cannot be defined in words.

entries.title: Daodejing
entries.description: Founding text of Daoism, traditionally attributed to Laozi.

entries.title: Dengyō Daishi
entries.description: Founder of the Japanese Tendai sect of Buddhism and of the Enryakuji monastery, also known as Saichō.

entries.title: densho
entries.description: Secret documents of a Ryū that record its techniques and rules.

entries.title: dō
entries.description: Term for the Asian worldview.

entries.title: dō no hi
entries.description: Another name for the pocket warmer dōka.

entries.title: dōka
entries.description: Pocket warmer, a small stove into which the ninja put a piece of smoldering charcoal. Also dō no hi.

entries.title: dokko-in
entries.translation: sign of the Tibetan vajra thunderbolt
entries.description: Hand sign for rin in kuji-in.

entries.title: doko no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: dōkyō
entries.description: Teaching and religion from China; in Japanese the philosophical school is more precisely called dōka (道家). It teaches a turn toward nature and an understanding of the universe.

entries.title: dosha
entries.description: Principle of gojō goyoku that exploits a person’s irritability.

entries.title: doteki
entries.description: Dynamics, the most effective application of mechanics (kikaigaku). It includes the proper use of energy, rhythm and flow, strength and flexibility, and the ability to feel an action and adapt to it.

entries.title: doton
entries.description: Escape by means of earth, one of the five methods of gotonpō.

entries.title: doton jutsu
entries.translation: the art of escaping with earth
entries.description: Escape technique from gotonpō that uses earth as a means of escape.

entries.title: Edo
entries.description: Former name of the Japanese capital, today Tōkyō.

entries.title: eiku
entries.description: Boat oar used as a weapon in Okinawan kobudō. A ninja disguised as a fisherman could put up a good defense with it.

entries.title: eki
entries.description: Consulted with coins or yarrow stalks, as in the Chinese <cite>I Ching</cite>.

entries.title: endoku ken
entries.description: Throwing star (shuriken) that could be set alight and then gave off poisonous gases.

entries.title: engetsu
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: ennyū no jutsu
entries.description: A squad stages a feint assault. While the defenders rush to meet it, the ninja slips into the fortress unhindered.

entries.title: Enryakuji
entries.description: Head monastery of the Tendai sect on Mount Hiei near Kyōto, founded at the behest of Tennō Kammu as the center of Tendai Buddhism. At its height, up to 40,000 monks and sōhei are said to have lived in 3,000 temples on the mountain. In September 1571, Oda Nobunaga destroyed the monastery during his campaign against the Ikkō ikki, the ninja, and the sōhei, and killed most of its inhabitants.

entries.title: fudō ken
entries.description: A way of making a fist found in many martial arts: the <q>normal</q> fist.

entries.title: fudōmyō
entries.description: Fudō Myōō, the fearsome mythical protector of the will, the laws, and the integrity of the universe. In kuji-kiri, the ninja imitates his flaming sword.

entries.title: fudōshin
entries.description: A calm, unshakable mind.

entries.title: fudōza no kamae
entries.description: Seated posture in Japan and also a stance (kamae) in ninjutsu.

entries.title: Fujibayashi Nagato
entries.description: Famous jōnin from the Iga region. According to a popular theory, just a false identity of Momochi Sandayū.

entries.title: Fujita Seiko
entries.description: Grandmaster of ninjutsu who called himself the 14th and last head of the Kōga-Ryū; he named no successor. He died in Tōkyō on January 4, 1966.

entries.title: fukibari
entries.description: Ninja fighting technique of blowing small metal needles (fukumi bari) into the attacker’s face.

entries.title: fukiya
entries.description: The darts were usually poisoned.

entries.title: fukumi bari
entries.description: Small metal needles blown in fukibari.

entries.title: fukuro gaeshi jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri. After what looks like a quarrel, the ninja changes sides and serves a new master for a while. When the war reaches a decisive phase, the ninja carries out the mission and returns to the old master.

entries.title: fukuro gaeshi zen jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of chikairi. The ninja intercepts messages between the enemy lord and his allies, forges them, and sends them on to sow distrust between them.

entries.title: Fūma Kotarō
entries.description: Famous ninja of jōnin rank with, according to tradition, 200 followers, a specialist in guerrilla warfare.

entries.title: furyō
entries.description: Good-for-nothings, young thugs.

entries.title: futokoro teppō
entries.description: Bronze pistol that was easy to conceal and popular with the ninja.

entries.title: gandō
entries.description: Lamp whose light source always stays upright.

entries.title: gankō
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: gasshō no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu, a greeting with the palms pressed together.

entries.title: gebaku ken-in
entries.description: Hand sign for kai in kuji-in, the same sign used in prayer.

entries.title: gedan no kamae
entries.description: Low stance (kamae).

entries.title: geinyū jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of chikairi. The ninja enters enemy territory to spread confusion, fear, and terror, for example with false rumors, arson, and sabotage.

entries.title: gekkenjutsu
entries.description: Sword fighting. Listed together with kenjutsu in the bugei jūhappan.

entries.title: genin
entries.description: Lowest rank of the ninja. These agents in the field took their orders from the chūnin and usually did not know the jōnin. Their strengths were close combat, concealment, infiltration, and sabotage.

entries.title: Genji
entries.description: Another name for the Minamoto.

entries.title: genmai
entries.description: Unpolished rice.

entries.title: Genpei kassen
entries.description: The Genpei War (1180–1185) between the Taira and the Minamoto.

entries.title: geri
entries.description: Also keri.

entries.title: geta
entries.description: Wooden sandals raised on tall supports, with a cross strap or a toe strap.

entries.title: gi
entries.description: Training clothes.

entries.title: Gikan-Ryū
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: gisō jutsu
entries.translation: the art of imitation and disguise
entries.description: The art of putting oneself in another person’s place and taking on a new identity. Part of onshin jutsu.

entries.title: godai
entries.description: The five elements of the universe in mikkyō: earth (chi), water (sui), fire (ka), wind (fū), and emptiness (kū).

entries.title: godan
entries.description: In the Bujinkan test for godan, the teacher approaches the student silently with a sword. The student has to sense the danger and evade the stroke.

entries.title: gogyō
entries.description: View of nature taken over from Chinese Daoism: water (sui), wood (moku), fire (ka), earth (do), and metal (kin).

entries.title: gogyō setsu
entries.description: Short form gogyō.

entries.title: gojō goyoku
entries.description: Ninja strategy of steering people through their character traits. Its five principles are aisha, dosha, kisha, kyōsha, and rakusha.

entries.title: goku no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: Gorin no sho
entries.description: Miyamoto Musashi’s work on swordsmanship and strategy.

entries.title: gorintō
entries.description: Stone monument of five stacked parts – cube, sphere, pyramid, half-moon, and jewel.

entries.title: goton jutsu
entries.description: Another name for gotonpō.

entries.title: gotonpō
entries.description: The ninja principle of escaping with the help of the five elements of gogyō.

entries.title: gunryaku heihō
entries.description: Military strategy. One of the 18 fields of the ninja jūhakkei.

entries.title: gyaku nagare
entries.description: Breakfall (ukemi) from ichimonji no kamae.

entries.title: gyaku nage
entries.description: Throw with a joint lock.

entries.title: gyōja no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) in which a long staff is held upright beside the body like a walking stick.

entries.title: gyōkaku ken
entries.description: The index, middle, and ring fingers form a trident whose tips stab into soft parts of the body such as the neck.

entries.title: Gyokko-Ryū
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: gyokuro
entries.description: High-grade green tea. Ninja are said to have made a poison from it by burying the tea in the ground for 30 to 40 days and then mixing it with soybean paste. A sick person died of it within a few days, a healthy one after 70 days at most.

entries.title: Gyokushin-Ryū
entries.translation: the school of the jeweled heart
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: gyorin
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: ha jutsu
entries.description: Escaping from holds.

entries.title: Hagakure
entries.description: Book by the samurai Yamamoto Tsunetomo on the philosophical side of bushidō.

entries.title: hakama
entries.description: Traditional divided skirt.

entries.title: han
entries.description: The fief of a daimyō.

entries.title: hanbō
entries.description: Its proper name is san shaku bō.

entries.title: hanbōjutsu
entries.description: Fighting with the short staff (hanbō).

entries.title: hankyū
entries.description: Short bow of the ninja, sometimes collapsible and easy to carry.

entries.title: hanmi no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: happō hiken
entries.description: The eight methods (happō) and the secret sword techniques (hiken) of the Kukishinden-Ryū.

entries.title: happō hikenjutsu
entries.description: See happō hiken.

entries.title: hara
entries.description: The whole area between the stomach and the lower abdomen, regarded as the center of mental and physical strength.

entries.title: hasami bune
entries.description: Collapsible ninja boat used to carry equipment across water. The Bansenshūkai describes such a folding boat as the hasamibako bune (挟箱船): its boards were joined by hinges, and folded up it fit into a carrying chest. Also tatami bune.

entries.title: hashigo
entries.description: Usually made of reed or bamboo. In compounds bashigo, as in kumo bashigo.

entries.title: hashigo yari
entries.description: Long pole with pegs projecting in pairs and an iron hook at the top, used as a ladder.

entries.title: Hatsumi Masaaki
entries.description: Born Hatsumi Yoshiaki. Founder of the Bujinkan Budō Dōjō, sōke of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan, and student of Takamatsu Toshitsugu.

entries.title: Hattori Hanzō
entries.description: Famous jōnin from the Iga region who was also a samurai in the service of Tokugawa Ieyasu.

entries.title: Hayes, Stephen K.
entries.description: Teacher of ninjutsu and student of Hatsumi Masaaki. He was the first non-Japanese to become a shidōshi. In the United States he founded the Tōshindō school.

entries.title: heihō
entries.description: Covers combat methods as well as combat strategies (bōryaku).

entries.title: Heike
entries.description: Another name for the Taira.

entries.title: heipo
entries.description: Ninja crawling method.

entries.title: hensō jutsu
entries.description: The ninja art of disguise. Part of onshin jutsu.

entries.title: hichō no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: hira ichimonji no kamae
entries.description: Balanced stance (kamae) from which the body can evade. The weight rests evenly on both feet, and both arms stretch out to the sides to sweep, grab, or catch blows.

entries.title: hira no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: hira shuriken
entries.description: Flat throwing stars (shuriken) in various sizes and shapes, with different numbers of points.

entries.title: hiragana
entries.description: Japanese syllabary used for purely Japanese words. According to tradition, Kōbō Daishi invented it.

entries.title: hiraki ashi
entries.description: Sliding sideways with both feet.

entries.title: hishi
entries.description: Dried water chestnuts that served the same purpose as a tetsubishi.

entries.title: hisoken
entries.description: Another name for shitō ken, in which the tip of the thumb stabs into semi-soft targets.

entries.title: hito washi
entries.description: Flying device of the ninja. Also yamidoko.

entries.title: hobakujutsu
entries.description: The art of binding. Listed together with hōjō jutsu in the bugei jūhappan.

entries.title: hōen
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: Hōjō
entries.description: Clan of samurai who rose to power, one of the families that fought for control during the Sengoku jidai.

entries.title: hojutsu
entries.description: The method of switching between truth and deception, which Hatsumi Masaaki equates with kyojitsu tenkan hō. In the bugei jūhappan it stands for illusions.

entries.title: hokamuri
entries.description: Cloth tied over the head and cheeks. Another name for the tenugui.

entries.title: hōkashi
entries.description: Musician. One of the ninja disguises in the shichi hō de.

entries.title: hōken jūroppō
entries.translation: sixteen methods of the precious fist

entries.title: Hokkaidō
entries.description: Northernmost island of Japan, with Sapporo as its capital.

entries.title: hōko no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: hōshi
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: hotarubi jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri. A messenger carrying a forged message is sent through enemy territory and allowed to be intercepted.

entries.title: iai jutsu
entries.description: The samurai art of killing an opponent with the first stroke, if possible.

entries.title: iaidō
entries.description: Sport developed from iai jutsu.

entries.title: iainuki
entries.description: Drawing the sword quickly, a specialty of the Shinden-Fudō-Ryū.

entries.title: ichi no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: ichimonji no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: Iga
entries.description: Japanese province near Kyōto where the ninja were especially active.

entries.title: Iga Ueno
entries.description: Town in the Iga region, once the center of the ninja. Today museums and festivals commemorate them.

entries.title: Iga Ueno-jō
entries.description: Iga Ueno Castle.

entries.title: iga dama
entries.description: Thistle, see tetsubishi.

entries.title: Iga-Ryū
entries.description: Ninjutsu style, today’s Kumogakure-Ryū.

entries.title: Igasaki Dōjun
entries.description: Famous ninja from Iga Province who got into an enemy castle with an astonishing ruse.

entries.title: ikkō ikki
entries.translation: uprising of the Jōdo Shinshū Buddhists
entries.description: Uprisings and leagues of followers of the Jōdo Shinshū school of Buddhism in the 15th and 16th centuries.

entries.title: in shin ton kei
entries.description: Principle of ninjutsu: the greatest effect with the least effort, changing the natural course of things as little as possible.

entries.title: innin
entries.description: Title of the fifth, sixth, and seventh volumes of the Bansenshūkai. They deal with the in, the dark side of ninja knowledge, with ruses, deception, and surprise attacks.

entries.title: inpō
entries.description: The art of concealment and camouflage.

entries.title: inton
entries.description: Another name for onshin jutsu, the art of hiding and camouflage.

entries.title: inton jutsu
entries.translation: the ninja art of escaping and hiding

entries.title: in’yō
entries.translation: cosmic dual forces, yin and yang, sun and moon
entries.description: The Japanese equivalent of yin and yang, the Daoist symbol of duality.

entries.title: ippon sugi nobori
entries.translation: a way of climbing a cedar
entries.description: Device for climbing a tree: a piece of iron with a hook, attached to two ropes with handles.

entries.title: Ishikawa Goemon
entries.description: Famous thief who according to legend was a ninja and used his art to steal, a kind of Japanese <q>Robin Hood</q>.

entries.title: jari bako
entries.description: Containers filled with rice, sand, or gravel, used to toughen the hands. Also kanshu.

entries.title: ji
entries.description: Another word for samurai.

entries.title: jihi no kokoro
entries.description: The mark of enlightenment in ninpō, stronger than love itself. It is born from walking the line between life and death again and again.

entries.title: jikatabi
entries.description: Ninja footwear with a separate big toe, especially suited to running and climbing silently.

entries.title: Jin ryaku no maki
entries.translation: scroll of the strategies of man
entries.description: Book on the strategies of man, part of a series with <cite>Ten ryaku no maki</cite> and <cite>Chi ryaku no maki</cite>.

entries.title: jitte
entries.description: Hand weapon with a hook for catching sword blows. Also jutte.

entries.title: jō
entries.description: The full name is yon shaku bō.

entries.title: jōei jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri. Shortly before hostilities break out, a ninja goes into enemy territory, where the general preparations for war make it easy to disappear, for example as a hired laborer or soldier.

entries.title: jōjutsu
entries.description: Fighting with the walking stick (jō). Part of the bugei jūhappan and the ninja jūhakkei.

entries.title: jōnin
entries.description: Highest rank of the ninja: the leader of a clan, whose true identity was usually known only to the chūnin. The jōnin gave the genin their tasks, and their strengths lay in politics, strategy, and philosophy.

entries.title: jū tai jutsu
entries.description: Grappling, joint locks, and chokes from the taijutsu of ninjutsu.

entries.title: jūdō
entries.description: Japanese martial sport that Professor Kanō Jigorō developed from jūjutsu in 1882.

entries.title: jūjutsu
entries.description: Old Japanese martial art of the samurai.

entries.title: jumon
entries.description: The charged word, the Japanese counterpart of the mantra. It embodies the intellect.

entries.title: jūmonji no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: jun nagare
entries.description: Breakfall (ukemi) from ichimonji no kamae.

entries.title: jūnantaisō
entries.description: Ninja exercises for agility and flexibility.

entries.title: jutte
entries.description: Hand weapon with a hook for catching sword blows. Also jitte.

entries.title: ka jutsu
entries.description: The use of fire, firearms, and explosives.

entries.title: kabuto
entries.description: Helmet of Japanese armor.

entries.title: kagi nawa
entries.description: Long rope with a hook at the end.

entries.title: kagi yari
entries.description: Ninja weapon used to fend off sword blows and to climb trees. Also kama yari.

entries.title: kaiki
entries.description: Title of the Bansenshūkai volume on tools for opening doors and locks and for breaking in. As another name for the tenugui, the word is not attested.

entries.title: kaki
entries.description: Title of the last volume of the <cite>Bansenshūkai</cite>, with formulas for explosives, smoke bombs, medicines, narcotics, and poisons.

entries.title: kakushi kokeshi
entries.description: Kokeshi doll hiding a weight, used as a weapon.

entries.title: kakuyoku
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: kama
entries.description: Tool used throughout Asia to cut grain, rice, or sugar cane.

entries.title: kama ikada
entries.description: One-person raft made of rushes.

entries.title: kama yari
entries.description: Ninja weapon used to fend off sword blows and to climb trees. Also kagi yari.

entries.title: kami gakure no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of hiding behind God
entries.description: Approaching a target by a roundabout route. The ninja befriends the relatives or confidants of a heavily guarded target and so gets close.

entries.title: kamikaze
entries.description: Name of the two typhoons that destroyed the Mongol forces under Kublai Khan. In World War II, the pilots who had to crash their planes into Allied ships and bases on suicide missions were also called kamikaze.

entries.title: kamiza
entries.description: The most important place in the dōjō, where pictures of the grandmaster hang and religious objects are sometimes displayed.

entries.title: kana
entries.description: The Japanese syllabaries, the umbrella term for hiragana and katakana. In everyday writing they are mixed with Chinese characters (kanji).

entries.title: kanji
entries.description: The Japanese adopted these characters, and they make up most of their script today.

entries.title: kanjin kaname
entries.description: What a person attains who leaves the material world behind and experiences the cosmic laws. The teaching of the Togakure-Ryū equates it with shinshin shingan (神心神眼), the mind and eyes of God.

entries.title: kanshu
entries.description: Containers filled with rice, sand, or gravel, used to toughen the hands. Also jari bako.

entries.title: kantō kusha
entries.description: Male instructor of a kunoichi.

entries.title: kanzashi
entries.description: Hairpin of wood or metal with two prongs like a fork.

entries.title: karate dō
entries.description: Martial art that originated on Okinawa, an island group in the south of Japan.

entries.title: kasha
entries.description: Pulley for rappelling.

entries.title: kasugai
entries.description: Clamp that ninja wedged onto doors to keep them from being opened.

entries.title: kata
entries.description: Prescribed sequence of movements.

entries.title: kata ashi tobi geri
entries.description: Jumping kick in which one foot drives into the opponent while the other knee is drawn up to the body.

entries.title: kataga hasami bune
entries.description: Small boat.

entries.title: katagatae jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of chikairi. When the enemy leaves camp, the ninja slips in, sabotages key installations, panics the remaining guards, and opens the gates for the ninja’s own troops.

entries.title: katakana
entries.description: Japanese syllabary, used mainly for foreign words, telegrams, and onomatopoeia.

entries.title: katana
entries.description: Long sword of the samurai with a curved, single-edged blade 61 to 76 centimeters long. Together with the wakizashi, it forms the daishō.

entries.title: katana kake
entries.description: Rack for the katana in the house. The wakizashi was only set down for sleeping or bathing, and even then it stayed within reach.

entries.title: katate
entries.description: One-handed, as in breakfalls (ukemi).

entries.title: Katō Danzō
entries.description: Famous ninja said to have been a master of jumping techniques.

entries.title: katon
entries.description: Escape by means of fire, one of the five methods of gotonpō.

entries.title: katon jutsu
entries.description: Escape technique from gotonpō that uses fire as a means of escape.

entries.title: katsura otoko jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri, named after an old Chinese tale. A ninja cut off from comrades in enemy country relies on the help of locals, the chitsu mishi, who give shelter and spy for the ninja.

entries.title: kayaku jutsu
entries.translation: the art of handling fire and explosives

entries.title: kayaku zutsu
entries.description: Sealed bamboo tubes for carrying gunpowder dry.

entries.title: ken
entries.description: The fist as a body weapon.

entries.title: kendō
entries.description: Martial sport that grew out of the swordsmanship (kenjutsu) of the samurai. Today a shinai replaces the sword, and armor is worn for protection.

entries.title: kenjutsu
entries.description: Swordsmanship of feudal Japan.

entries.title: kenpō
entries.description: Unarmed fighting method, listed with jūjutsu in the bugei jūhappan.

entries.title: kensei
entries.description: A person who had fully grasped the essence of the Way and was considered almost invincible. The best-known example is Miyamoto Musashi.

entries.title: kenshō
entries.description: Understanding of all things, enlightenment, also satori.

entries.title: keri
entries.description: Also geri.

entries.title: ketsuin
entries.description: The hand position, the Japanese counterpart of the mudrā. It embodies physical action.

entries.title: kiai
entries.description: Release of energy in a battle cry, which should accompany an effective technique. Legends tell of masters who killed small animals with the shout and paralyzed people for a moment; all that can be shown is that a sudden shout startles an opponent for an instant.

entries.title: kiai jutsu
entries.translation: the art of the battle cry
entries.description: The art of using the kiai.

entries.title: Kido Yazaemon
entries.description: Famous ninja who tried to assassinate Oda Nobunaga and failed.

entries.title: kigomi
entries.description: Armor worn under ordinary clothes, such as a kusari katabira; some quilted versions also had lacquered plates. Warriors and travelers wore it; there is no evidence that ninja wore it regularly.

entries.title: kikaigaku
entries.description: The body’s most effective responses to an attack, including footwork, sidestepping, fighting distance, and the proper use of the body weapons.

entries.title: kinton
entries.description: Escape by means of metal, one of the five methods of gotonpō.

entries.title: kinton jutsu
entries.description: Escape technique from gotonpō that uses metal as a means of escape.

entries.title: kisha
entries.description: Principle of gojō goyoku that exploits a person’s vanity.

entries.title: kishaku
entries.description: Floating compass: a magnetized piece of iron, often shaped like a fish or a boat, floating in a bowl of water. The principle came from China; the <cite>Bansenshūkai</cite> explains how to make such a compass.

entries.title: kiten
entries.description: From a crouch over the hands into a handstand, then through a bridge back onto the feet.

entries.title: kitsune gakure no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of hiding like a fox
entries.description: Technique of hiding in the reeds like a fox.

entries.title: ko ashi
entries.description: Ninja way of walking.

entries.title: Kōbō Daishi
entries.description: Founder of the esoteric Buddhist Shingon sect, also known as Kūkai.

entries.title: kobudō
entries.description: Weapon system developed on Okinawa that uses mostly farm tools as weapons.

entries.title: kobujutsu jūhappan
entries.description: Martial arts that Hatsumi Masaaki practiced for three years under Ueno Sensei.

entries.title: kodachi
entries.description: Short sword.

entries.title: kodachijutsu
entries.description: Fighting with the short sword (kodachi), part of bikenjutsu.

entries.title: Kōga-Ryū
entries.description: Ninjutsu style, most likely extinct today.

entries.title: kōgai
entries.description: Pin fitted to the side of the wakizashi. It served as a tool for repairing leather goods or caring for hooves.

entries.title: kogakure
entries.description: The author chose this name for this website.

entries.title: kōhō ukemi
entries.description: Breakfall (ukemi) to the rear. From standing, you sink into a deep crouch and roll back onto your back.

entries.title: kokizami ashi
entries.description: Ninja way of walking.

entries.title: koku
entries.description: Japanese measure of volume for rice. In feudal Japan, people were paid in koku; one koku is about 180 liters of rice.

entries.title: kokū
entries.description: Empty space, the void.

entries.title: kokyūhō
entries.description: Methods of proper breathing.

entries.title: komusō
entries.description: Mendicant monk of the Fuke order. The komusō wandered through Japan wearing a white kimono, a large hat that covered the whole face, a sword (katana), a long walking staff, a fan, and a flute (shakuhachi). They were never allowed to take off their hats or to speak in the presence of anyone but monks. Officially the sect no longer exists, but it may live on underground.

entries.title: kongō
entries.description: Short metal weapon that Buddhist priests used for self-defense. The scepter symbolizes the diamond, the sign of pure knowledge. Also known as Indra’s weapon.

entries.title: kongōkai mandara
entries.description: Strictly geometric mandala with Buddhas and deities arranged in nine sections.

entries.title: kongōsho
entries.description: Buddhist ritual implement (vajra) with three prongs curving inward at each end.

entries.title: koppō jutsu
entries.description: Bone-breaking techniques. Hard training strengthened the hands and feet to deliver devastating blows against the bones.

entries.title: kōsei no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) from ninjutsu.

entries.title: koshi jutsu
entries.description: Techniques against the muscles of the body that cause severe pain.

entries.title: koshizashi
entries.description: Early hand firearm that Suginobō Myōsan was shown on Tanegashima and had copied.

entries.title: Kotō-Ryū
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: kōyaku
entries.description: Battle formation from the bōryaku.

entries.title: kū
entries.description: Origin of subatomic energy, nothingness, the beginning of all things.

entries.title: ku shaku bō
entries.description: Extra-long staff (2.73 meters).

entries.title: kubotan
entries.description: Fist weapon in the shape of a small cylinder, used to apply pressure to joints.

entries.title: kuden
entries.description: Passing on the martial arts by word of mouth rather than in writing.

entries.title: kūhen no kata
entries.translation: forms of the transformation of emptiness

entries.title: kuji goshin hō
entries.description: Another name for kuji-kiri.

entries.title: kuji-in
entries.description: The nine finger signs (mudrā) used by the ninja.

entries.title: kuji-in jin
entries.description: Sixth seal of the kuji-in. It shows a person who relies entirely on God’s cosmic consciousness and trusts their intuition.

entries.title: kuji-in kai
entries.description: Fifth seal of the kuji-in. It shows a person striving to come close to God. Its hand sign is the gebaku ken-in.

entries.title: kuji-in pyō
entries.description: Second seal of the kuji-in, the physical symbol of the diamond and so of knowledge. Its hand sign is the daikongō-in.

entries.title: kuji-in retsu
entries.description: Seventh seal of the kuji-in. Its hand sign is the chiken-in.

entries.title: kuji-in rin
entries.description: First seal of the kuji-in. It stands for kongō, the diamond-like thunderbolt. Its hand sign is the dokko-in.

entries.title: kuji-in sha
entries.description: Fourth seal of the kuji-in.

entries.title: kuji-in tō
entries.description: Third seal of the kuji-in. Its hand sign is the sotojishi-in.

entries.title: kuji-in zai
entries.description: Eighth seal of the kuji-in. It symbolizes the fire that destroys all impurities and makes the mind one with the universe.

entries.title: kuji-in zen
entries.description: Ninth seal of the kuji-in. It symbolizes the fully enlightened one who has seen through all things.

entries.title: kuji-kiri
entries.description: Ritual of drawing a protective grid in the air with a symbolic sword. Not to be confused with kuji-in.

entries.title: Kūkai
entries.description: Another name for Kōbō Daishi.

entries.title: Kukishinden-Ryū
entries.translation: the school of the nine demon gods
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: kumade
entries.description: Ninja weapon that could inflict terrible wounds. It was also used for climbing.

entries.title: Kumawaka
entries.description: Famous genin of the Kōga-Ryū who led 70 ninja guerrillas.

entries.title: Kumogakure-Ryū
entries.translation: the school of the hidden cloud
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: kunoichi
entries.description: Female ninja. According to tradition, they were trained in close combat like their male comrades, but their focus was on influencing the human mind.

entries.title: kunoichi jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri that uses women as agents to get close to key men.

entries.title: Kuroi Ōkami
entries.description: Name of the Bujinkan dōjō in Wolfsburg, led by shidōshi Mario Plückhahn.

entries.title: kuruma nagare
entries.description: Breakfall (ukemi), rolling backward (kōhō kuruma nagare).

entries.title: kusari fundō
entries.description: Short chain with a weight at each end.

entries.title: kusari katabira
entries.description: Chain mail that ninja wore in battle under or over the shinobi shōzoku. The mesh also protected the face and palms.

entries.title: kusarigama
entries.description: Japanese sickle (kama) with a weighted chain (kusari).

entries.title: kusarijutsu
entries.description: Fighting with short chain weapons.

entries.title: kyobako fune
entries.description: A wooden box covered with leather on the outside.

entries.title: kyojitsu tenkan hō
entries.description: Tactic of presenting the truth as a lie and the lie as the truth, for example showing strength when weak.

entries.title: kyoketsu shōge
entries.description: A favorite weapon of the ninja. A knife with a hook, with a four-meter rope attached to the handle and a steel ring at its end.

entries.title: kyōmon
entries.description: Practical education, observation, and common sense. One of the eight disciplines of the ninja no hachimon.

entries.title: kyōnin no jutsu
entries.description: Tactic that exploits people’s superstitions, for example with devil masks, fire-breathing, or animals thought to be evil.

entries.title: kyōsha
entries.description: Principle of gojō goyoku that exploits a person’s cowardice.

entries.title: Kyōto
entries.description: Old Japanese imperial city.

entries.title: kyūdō
entries.description: Sport developed from the martial kyūjutsu.

entries.title: kyūjutsu
entries.description: The samurai method of shooting with bow and arrow.

entries.title: kyūsho
entries.description: The pressure points for atemi. The Kotō-Ryū contains their complete system.

entries.title: li
entries.description: In Daoism, the structure and form of the Dao: an asymmetrical order that never repeats itself and follows no rule. It shows in flowing water, tree bark, or ice crystals.

entries.title: Lin Kuei
entries.description: Supposed name under which ninjutsu is said to have existed in China and Korea; there is no historical evidence for it.

entries.title: maai
entries.description: Harmonious distance in time and space.

entries.title: mamukigama
entries.description: Sickle with a rope, at the end of which hung a venomous animal such as a snake. The ninja hurled it at the enemy; the animal kept the opponent busy and might even kill them.

entries.title: mandala
entries.description: Schematic image of the universe, from Tantra and mikkyō. In the sanmitsu, it stands for thought.

entries.title: mangetsu no kamae
entries.description: Stance of the Kotō-Ryū. The fighter holds the sword above the head so that sunlight on the blade dazzles the opponent.

entries.title: manriki gusari
entries.description: Chain with iron grips at the ends.

entries.title: mantra
entries.description: Sounds from Tantrism and mikkyō. In the sanmitsu, the mantra stands for the word.

entries.title: menkyo kaiden
entries.description: Certificate of complete mastery of a martial art. The master gave it to one or more students; it identifies the holder as the rightful heir of the style.

entries.title: metsubushi
entries.description: Blinding powder made of iron filings, sand, ash, or chemicals. When pursued, the ninja threw it into the pursuer’s eyes.

entries.title: mikkyō
entries.description: Umbrella term for various tantric teachings of Buddhism.

entries.title: miko
entries.description: Young, unmarried woman in the service of a Shintō shrine. According to tradition, Mochizuki Chiyome trained orphaned girls as miko and at the same time as kunoichi who spied for the Takeda family.

entries.title: Minamoto
entries.description: Famous family, also called Genji, that was at war with the Taira.

entries.title: minomushi jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri described in the Bansenshūkai: the ninja incited the enemy’s servants to betray their lord. The higher their rank, the more valuable they were.

entries.title: Miyamoto Musashi
entries.description: Japan’s most famous swordsman. He traveled the country for many years to improve his swordsmanship and won more than 60 duels along the way. He founded the Niten-Ichi-Ryū, a school that fights with two swords at once. Shortly before his death he wrote <cite>Gorin no sho</cite> (<q>The Book of Five Rings</q>).

entries.title: mizu taimatsu
entries.description: Torch that keeps burning in the rain.

entries.title: mizu tsutsu
entries.description: Reed or wooden tube through which the ninja breathed when staying under water for a long time.

entries.title: mizugumo
entries.description: Ninja tool for walking across marshland.

entries.title: Mochizuki Chiyome
entries.description: Famous kunoichi who, according to tradition, ran a network of kunoichi on behalf of Takeda Shingen.

entries.title: mokuton
entries.description: Escape by means of wood and plants, one of the five methods of gotonpō.

entries.title: mokuton jutsu
entries.description: Escape technique of gotonpō that uses wood as a means of escape.

entries.title: monomi no jutsu
entries.description: Scouting the weak points of an enemy’s defenses, such as easily entered rooms, back doors, and unused rooms.

entries.title: Mōri
entries.description: Samurai clan from Aki in western Honshū, one of the families that fought for power in the Sengoku period. Under Mōri Motonari it came to rule the Chūgoku region and later stood against Oda Nobunaga.

entries.title: mu
entries.description: Also bu.

entries.title: mudrā
entries.description: Hand positions from Tantra and mikkyō. Nine of them were adopted into the kuji-in. In the sanmitsu, they stand for action.

entries.title: mumei mugei no jutsu
entries.description: The art of anonymity, the ninja’s recipe for success in espionage. No one was to know the ninja’s true face.

entries.title: musha dori
entries.description: Secret technique of the Musashi-Ryū. Takamatsu Toshitsugu learned it at the age of 15 in a fight against a karateka of that school.

entries.title: musha shugyō
entries.description: Method of training in which the warrior set out on a long journey to improve. The hardships along the way shaped character and strengthened the spirit.

entries.title: musubi bashigo
entries.description: Rope with loops at fixed intervals, into which the ninja put the feet when climbing.

entries.title: musubi nawa
entries.description: Horsehair rope.

entries.title: mute
entries.description: Without hands, as in breakfalls (ukemi).

entries.title: nagamaki
entries.description: A variant of the naginata sword lance.

entries.title: nagare
entries.description: Principle of softness.

entries.title: nage teppō
entries.description: Explosive grenade thrown at the enemy by hand or with a sling. It worked like a modern hand grenade.

entries.title: nagenawa
entries.description: Lasso. The Gyokushin-Ryū is known for its use.

entries.title: naginata
entries.description: Sword lance, a weapon of the sōhei and the favorite weapon of samurai women.

entries.title: naginatadō
entries.description: Martial art of the naginata, practiced mainly by women after World War II.

entries.title: nagishi shuriken
entries.description: Throwing star (shuriken) with a tassel at the end that stabilizes its flight.

entries.title: naibaku ken-in
entries.translation: sign of the inner bound fist
entries.description: Hand sign for jin in kuji-in.

entries.title: neko te
entries.description: Pointed thimble, a weapon of the kunoichi.

entries.title: nenriki
entries.description: Focused intention, the Japanese counterpart of the mandala. It embodies the ninja’s will.

entries.title: nichirin-in
entries.description: Hand sign for zai in kuji-in.

entries.title: Nihon
entries.description: Japan. Also Nippon.

entries.title: nin
entries.translation: to endure, to bear, to persevere, to avoid
entries.description: Also shinobu.

entries.title: nin shokudai
entries.description: L-shaped torch that could be hung up.

entries.title: ninja
entries.description: Practitioner of ninjutsu: fighter, scout, spy, guerrilla, and special agent of the feudal Middle Ages.

entries.title: ninja aruki
entries.description: The ninja’s ways of walking, to move silently, unseen, or fast.

entries.title: ninja jūhakkei
entries.description: The 18 categories of secret techniques a ninja learned in addition to the bugei jūhappan. Together the two make up the ninpō sanjūrokkei.

entries.title: ninja ken
entries.description: Also ninja tō.

entries.title: ninja tō
entries.description: Also ninja ken.

entries.title: ninjutsu
entries.description: Collective term for all Ryū practiced by the ninja. They often include unconventional and secret fighting techniques.

entries.title: ninki
entries.description: Part of the <cite>Bansenshūkai</cite> that describes the equipment. It begins in the ninth volume and runs into the final volume.

entries.title: ninniku yoroi
entries.description: Another name for shinobi shōzoku, the ninja’s suit.

entries.title: ninpō
entries.description: Ninjutsu as a way of life. Ninpō goes beyond technique and also teaches a spiritual path.

entries.title: ninpō ikkan
entries.translation: ninjutsu is the beginning and has no end

entries.title: ninpō inu bue
entries.description: The ninja’s art of training animals.

entries.title: ninpō mikkyō
entries.description: The secret teachings of the ninja, based on mikkyō.

entries.title: ninpō sanjūrokkei
entries.description: The 36 fields a ninja studied: the 18 martial arts of the bugei jūhappan and the 18 secret techniques of the ninja jūhakkei. The list was not fixed; fields were often dropped and others added.

entries.title: ninpō taijutsu
entries.description: Unarmed combat of the ninja. It also includes other physical skills such as breakfalls.

entries.title: Nippon
entries.description: Japan. Also Nihon.

entries.title: Nishina Daisuke
entries.description: Birth name of Togakure Daisuke, the founder of the Togakure-Ryū.

entries.title: nodachi
entries.description: Very long samurai sword, 1–1.80 meters long, usually carried by a servant.

entries.title: nunchaku
entries.description: Weapon from kobudō: two pieces of wood joined by a short chain or cord. Whether a ninja ever used it is highly doubtful.

entries.title: nuntebō
entries.description: Fishing spear: a fisherman’s tool that could also be used as a weapon.

entries.title: nyūdaki no jutsu
entries.description: Exploiting the weaknesses of guards, such as laziness or stupidity.

entries.title: nyūkyo no jutsu
entries.description: Waiting for the right moment to enter an enemy castle or camp, for example when the army had left on a campaign.

entries.title: Oda Nobunaga
entries.description: Military dictator who tried to seize power in Japan during the Sengoku period. The ruthless commander held central Japan, built a castle near Kyōto, and used European firearms without hesitation. After his death, his generals succeeded in unifying Japan.

entries.title: ōgama
entries.description: Much larger battlefield version of the kusarigama.

entries.title: Okinawa
entries.description: Group of islands in southern Japan.

entries.title: ōmetsuke
entries.description: Officials of the bakufu in the state police. They commanded the ninja who served in the secret police after the civil wars ended.

entries.title: omote soku gyaku ken no keri
entries.sort: Omote soku gyaku ken no keri
entries.description: Kick with the sole of the foot turned inward. The foot swings from the outside to the center line in front of your own body and meets the opponent on that line, for example on the inner thigh.

entries.title: ongyō no mono
entries.description: Byname of the ninja from Kōga.

entries.title: ongyō-in
entries.description: Hand sign for zen in kuji-in.

entries.title: oni kudaki
entries.description: Joint lock.

entries.title: onibi
entries.description: Gruesome wooden mask the ninja used to terrify pursuers.

entries.title: ono gama
entries.description: Combined weapon of battle-ax and sickle.

entries.title: onshin jutsu
entries.description: The ninja’s art of hiding, camouflage, and becoming invisible.

entries.title: ōtsuchi
entries.description: War hammer, a weapon of the Shinden-Fudō-Ryū.

entries.title: rakusha
entries.description: Principle of gojō goyoku that exploits a person’s laziness.

entries.title: rappa
entries.description: Another name for ninja, such as the guerrillas who followed Fūma Kotarō. Also suppa.

entries.title: roku shaku bō
entries.description: The most common form of the bō, about 1.82 meters long. Roku means six, and shaku is a Japanese unit of length.

entries.title: rōnin
entries.description: Masterless samurai. Samurai who had lost their lord (daimyō) roamed the country. Some hired themselves out as mercenaries, others became martial arts teachers, and some became robbers who plundered farmers.

entries.title: ryakuhon jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of chikairi: the ninja slipped into the enemy camp and posed as an ally. This required that the ninja was already known there and knew the area well.

entries.title: ryō ashi tobi geri
entries.description: Jumping kick in which the fighter takes off from both legs and keeps them together. The full force of the body hits the opponent.

entries.title: ryō yoku geri
entries.description: Kick used mostly when the fighter jumps down on the opponent from a raised position.

entries.title: ryōhan jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of chikairi: the ninja kidnapped a key figure to enforce demands. Other key figures had to serve the ninja, or the victim would be executed.

entries.title: ryōte
entries.description: Two-handed, as in breakfalls (ukemi).

entries.title: ryūha
entries.translation: school of a style or tradition
entries.description: Longer form of Ryū.

entries.title: sai
entries.description: Weapon from kobudō.

entries.title: Saichō
entries.description: Another name for Dengyō Daishi.

entries.title: Saiga Magoichi
entries.description: Leader of the Saika gunners, often counted among the ninja, with special skills in firearms and explosives. His men were good snipers. He developed the shaki no jutsu.

entries.title: sakki
entries.description: The Bujinkan test for fifth dan is named after it: the student has to evade a sword without seeing it. Hatsumi Masaaki took it under Takamatsu Toshitsugu.

entries.title: sakki jutsu
entries.translation: the art of guessing the mind
entries.description: Intuitive sight that lets the fighter evade a blow before it is delivered.

entries.title: samurai
entries.description: Japanese warrior class.

entries.title: san shaku bō
entries.description: Stick three shaku long, about 91 centimeters. Another name is hanbō.

entries.title: san shitan ken
entries.description: Variant of shitan ken with three fingers.

entries.title: sanmitsu
entries.description: The three powers of mikkyō: thought, word, and action. They are represented by the mandala, the mantra, and the mudrā.

entries.title: sanmyaku
entries.description: Name of the official Bujinkan magazine.

entries.title: sanpō hiden
entries.description: The three secret treasures of the Togakure-Ryū: the senban shuriken throwing star, the shukō claws, and the shindake bamboo tube.

entries.title: sansa jutsu
entries.description: Running techniques of the ninja.

entries.title: sashi ashi
entries.description: Cross step.

entries.title: satobito jutsu
entries.description: Tactic of tōiri: the ninja recruited a discontented, greedy, or ambitious subject of the enemy ruler. Such people supplied information, kept escape routes open, or provided materials.

entries.title: seigan no kamae
entries.description: Stance aimed at the opponent’s eyes.

entries.title: Seii taishōgun
entries.description: Originally the title of the army’s commander in chief, later shortened to shōgun.

entries.title: seishin teki kyōyō
entries.description: The first of the 18 disciplines of the ninja jūhakkei.

entries.title: seiza no kamae
entries.description: Kneeling, a stance (kamae) of ninjutsu.

entries.title: Sekigahara
entries.description: Small village in Mino province where Tokugawa Ieyasu won the final victory over his enemies.

entries.title: senban
entries.description: Four-pointed throwing star (shuriken).

entries.title: senban shaken
entries.description: Throwing star (shuriken) with a hole in the middle.

entries.title: Sengoku jidai
entries.description: The period of bloody civil wars in Japan, roughly 1467–1615.

entries.title: senjō jutsu
entries.description: Maneuvering troops.

entries.title: senjutsu
entries.description: Military strategy.

entries.title: sensei
entries.description: Teacher.

entries.title: shaken
entries.description: Multi-pointed throwing star (shuriken).

entries.title: shaki no jutsu
entries.description: Ruse of Saiga Magoichi at the battle of Naniwa Kanzakigawa: his men left their own flags behind and took up their new position under forged flags of Oda Nobunaga, whose troops took them for allies.

entries.title: shaku
entries.description: Japanese unit of length. One shaku is 30.3 centimeters (10/33 of a meter).

entries.title: shakuhachi
entries.description: Flute of the komusō. The name means one shaku eight sun, about 54.5 centimeters; the standard flute has five finger holes.

entries.title: shakujō
entries.description: Priest’s staff with rings at the end. Their jingling as the monk walked was meant to drive crawling creatures off the path, so that Buddhist monks could keep the precept against killing.

entries.title: shi shitan ken
entries.description: Variant of shitan ken, supported by the thumb.

entries.title: shiatsu
entries.description: Japanese massage that is said to relieve or cure fainting and other ailments by pressure on certain points of the body.

entries.title: shiba gakure no jutsu
entries.description: Technique of onshin jutsu from the Iga and Kōga traditions: hiding in dense brush, tall grass, or piles of firewood.

entries.title: shichi hō de
entries.description: The seven traditional disguises of the ninja.

entries.title: shidōshi
entries.description: Teacher of the warrior art of enlightenment.

entries.title: shihan
entries.description: In 1695, Emperor Higashiyama appointed Takagi Oriemon Shigenobu shihan of the imperial guard.

entries.title: shihō tenchi tobi
entries.translation: jumping in four directions, toward heaven and earth

entries.title: shiken haramitsu daikōmyō
entries.description: Words spoken at the beginning of a training session. In very simple terms, they mean <q>We ask for protection and enlightenment</q>.

entries.title: shikomizue
entries.description: Sword hidden in a staff.

entries.title: shikoro
entries.description: Thin saw the ninja used to get through wooden walls and doors.

entries.title: Shimabara no ran
entries.description: Uprising of the Christians in 1637–1638 on the Shimabara Peninsula. It was really a peasant revolt, which served as a pretext for persecuting Christians.

entries.title: shinai
entries.description: Sword made of several bamboo staves held together and tightened with leather and cords. It is used in kendō.

entries.title: shinbō
entries.description: Fist weapon with a ring for the middle finger.

entries.title: Shinden-Fudō-Ryū
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: shingitai
entries.description: One of the most important principles of the martial arts.

entries.title: Shingon
entries.description: Buddhist sect founded by Kōbō Daishi.

entries.title: shinobi
entries.translation: sneaking in, spying, entering by stealth, enduring
entries.description: Short form of ninja.

entries.title: shinobi bune
entries.description: Light, narrow boat.

entries.title: shinobi iri
entries.description: The ninja’s techniques for moving silently.

entries.title: shinobi jutsu
entries.description: Collective term for the various arts of the ninja.

entries.title: shinobi kai
entries.description: Hollow bamboo staff holding iron parts that could quickly be assembled into a paddle.

entries.title: shinobi katana
entries.description: Sword of the ninja.

entries.title: shinobi kenpō
entries.description: Swordsmanship of the ninja.

entries.title: shinobi no buki
entries.description: The weapons of the ninja.

entries.title: shinobi no jutsu
entries.description: Collective term for the various arts of the ninja. According to tradition, the name arose under Shōtoku Taishi.

entries.title: shinobi shobō
entries.description: Fist weapon and forerunner of the brass knuckles: the middle finger goes through a steel ring, and the rest of the weapon lies hidden in the fist.

entries.title: shinobi shōzoku
entries.description: Dark combat suit of the ninja, light gray or white in winter. Also ninniku yoroi.

entries.title: shinobi tantō
entries.description: Dagger (tantō) hidden in a staff.

entries.title: shinobi yari
entries.description: Spear of the ninja.

entries.title: shinobi zue
entries.description: Hollow bamboo staff with hidden weapons or blinding powder inside.

entries.title: shinobu
entries.translation: perseverance, forbearance, patience, self-control, to endure, to conceal, spy, to sneak

entries.title: Shintō
entries.description: Japanese religion that sees higher spirits in all forms of existence. Also called <q>Shintoism</q>.

entries.title: shishi undō
entries.description: Movement of the arms and legs.

entries.title: shizen ken
entries.description: The body’s natural weapons, such as the shoulder, body weight, or nails.

entries.title: shizen no kamae
entries.description: Stance (kamae) of ninjutsu.

entries.title: shizentai
entries.description: Relaxed, natural stance.

entries.title: shobō
entries.description: Fist weapon.

entries.title: shōgun
entries.description: Military commander of Japan.

entries.title: shoshin go gata
entries.translation: five forms of the beginner’s mind

entries.title: shōten
entries.description: Running up vertical surfaces, an ukemi exercise.

entries.title: shōten no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of climbing to heaven
entries.description: Running up a wall, a fence, a tree, or a person. With enough momentum, you jump at the obstacle, push off with the legs, and leap over it. A drill from modern training, also shōten jutsu.

entries.title: Shōtoku Taishi
entries.description: Prince regent (574–622). He is said to have been the first to use agents to learn the truth behind disputes.

entries.title: shugendō
entries.description: Esoteric teaching and form of asceticism practiced mainly by the yamabushi.

entries.title: shukō
entries.description: Claws for climbing and fighting, one of the three secret treasures of the Togakure-Ryū. Also tekagi.

entries.title: shuriken
entries.description: Throwing blades of the ninja, in all shapes and sizes.

entries.title: shutō ken
entries.description: Strike with the edge of the hand, the same strike as kiten ken.

entries.title: sodezutsu
entries.description: Hand cannon.

entries.title: sōhei
entries.description: Warrior monks and mercenaries in the service of monasteries.

entries.title: sōke
entries.description: Head of a Ryū.

entries.title: soku gyaku ken
entries.description: Kick with the tips of the toes into soft targets such as the belly or neck; a Bujinkan term.

entries.title: soku yaku ken
entries.description: Kick with the heel and sole into semi-soft or hard targets, for example down onto the knee; a Bujinkan term.

entries.title: sokuhō geri
entries.description: Kick in which the leg strikes out to the side while the upper body stays facing forward.

entries.title: sokuhō kiten
entries.description: Sideways handspring, an ukemi exercise.

entries.title: sokuhō tobi
entries.description: Low leap to the side, an ukemi exercise.

entries.title: sokuyaku suitei ken
entries.description: The leg kicks forward horizontally, and the foot hits the target from the side.

entries.title: Sonshi
entries.description: Japanese name for Sun Tzu, who according to tradition wrote <cite>The Art of War</cite> in the 6th century BC. The work reached Japan early and is said to have shaped the beginnings of ninjutsu.

entries.title: Sugitani Zenjūbō
entries.description: Famous ninja who tried to kill Oda Nobunaga with two bullets in 1570. Both only hit his shoulder pad.

entries.title: suikatsugan
entries.description: Pill against thirst made from pickled-plum flesh, sugar, and dwarf lilyturf root; the <cite>Bansenshūkai</cite> records the recipe. It kept the mouth and throat moist.

entries.title: suiki
entries.description: Section of the ninth volume of the <cite>Bansenshūkai</cite> on water equipment. It draws largely on advice from pirates and shows how to cross rivers or move under water.

entries.title: suiren
entries.description: Staying and moving under water.

entries.title: suiton
entries.description: Escape by means of water, one of the five methods of gotonpō.

entries.title: suiton jutsu
entries.description: Escape technique of gotonpō that uses water as a means of escape.

entries.title: suppa
entries.description: Another name for ninja, such as the guerrillas who followed Fūma Kotarō or served the Takeda family. Also rappa.

entries.title: tabi
entries.description: Japanese toe socks with the big toe separated from the other toes.

entries.title: tachi
entries.description: Sword similar to the katana, usually more strongly curved and carried on the battlefield. Ceremonially decorated and very elaborately crafted.

entries.title: tachi nagare
entries.description: Form of nagare: falling backward from a standing position.

entries.title: tai sabaki
entries.description: Movement of the trunk.

entries.title: taihen jutsu
entries.translation: the art of changing the body
entries.description: Part of taijutsu: stances, postures, movements, and falling techniques.

entries.title: taijutsu
entries.description: Unarmed combat.

entries.title: taikai
entries.description: Gathering of fighters at events.

entries.title: Taira
entries.description: Famous family, also called Heike, that was at war with the Minamoto.

entries.title: taizōkai mandara
entries.description: In the sanmitsu, it represents the material world, the world of the fertile ground.

entries.title: taka bashigo
entries.description: Ladder the ninja used to cross chasms. An extra rope reinforced its middle.

entries.title: Takagi-Yōshin-Ryū
entries.translation: school of the high tree willow spirit
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: Takamatsu Toshitsugu
entries.description: Teacher of various ninjutsu styles and master of Hatsumi Masaaki. The collection of the nine Ryū is called <q>Bujinkan</q> in his honor.

entries.title: Takeda Shingen
entries.description: Famous general (daimyō) who fought a series of wars in the Sengoku period.

entries.title: tanagokoro
entries.description: Palm torch that was especially useful for breaking open door locks.

entries.title: tanegashima
entries.description: Arquebus brought to Japan by the Portuguese. Also teppō.

entries.title: tantō
entries.description: Dagger.

entries.title: tantōjutsu
entries.description: Knife fighting techniques.

entries.title: tantra
entries.description: Current of Indian philosophy and religion, originally an esoteric form of Hinduism, later adopted into Tibetan Buddhism.

entries.title: tanuki gakure no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of hiding like a raccoon dog
entries.description: Ninja climbing technique: scaling trees and poles and hiding up high.

entries.title: taru ikada
entries.description: Ninja water tool made of two barrels: one foot went into each, and the ninja moved across the water with a paddle. Also uki daru.

entries.title: tatami
entries.description: Floor covering in Japanese houses and in the dōjō.

entries.title: tatami bune
entries.description: Another name for the hasami bune.

entries.title: tatami gama
entries.description: Sickle (kama) with a wooden handle whose curved blade folds open. The name is a modern description and does not appear in the ninja manuals.

entries.title: tebukuro
entries.description: Garment that covered the backs of the ninja’s hands and the forearms.

entries.title: tekagi
entries.description: Also shukō.

entries.title: tekken
entries.description: Brass knuckles. Also tekkō.

entries.title: tekkō
entries.description: Brass knuckles. Also tekken.

entries.title: Tendai
entries.description: Esoteric Buddhist sect of mikkyō, founded in Japan by Dengyō Daishi. Its center was the Enryakuji monastery on Mount Hiei.

entries.title: tengu
entries.description: Mythical creatures of Japanese tradition who lived in the mountains: with raven beaks and wings (karasu tengu or ko tengu) or in human form with long red noses (dai tengu). They were seen partly as protectors, partly as tricksters and dangerous. According to legend they were masters of the martial arts, and they are often regarded as the teachers of a style.

entries.title: tennō
entries.description: The Japanese emperor.

entries.title: tenugui
entries.description: Cotton cloth the ninja tied into a mask.

entries.title: teppō
entries.description: Another name for the tanegashima.

entries.title: tetsu mari
entries.description: Hollow iron ball with long spikes pointing in all directions, similar to the iga dama. The name is a modern description and does not appear in the ninja manuals.

entries.title: tetsubishi
entries.description: Iron caltrops that the ninja scattered on the ground in large numbers to stop pursuers.

entries.title: tōami
entries.description: Net the ninja could use to catch opponents.

entries.title: tobi ashi
entries.description: Ninja walking technique.

entries.title: tobi bashigo
entries.description: Ladder with hooks at the ends that could be thrown.

entries.title: tobi geri
entries.description: Kick delivered from a jump, such as kata ashi tobi geri or ryō ashi tobi geri.

entries.title: tobi ori
entries.description: Ukemi exercise: jumping down from a height.

entries.title: tobikunai
entries.description: Tool for opening locked gates.

entries.title: Toda Shinryūken Masamitsu
entries.description: Ninja master and teacher of Takamatsu Toshitsugu.

entries.title: Togakure Daisuke
entries.description: Founder of the Togakure-Ryū. He fled to the Iga region after a lost battle.

entries.title: Togakure-Ryū
entries.description: One of the nine Ryū of the Bujinkan.

entries.title: tōiri
entries.description: Strategy the ninja used preventively in peacetime, mainly espionage.

entries.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu
entries.description: Famous daimyō and ally of Oda Nobunaga. After the end of the Sengoku period, he was appointed shōgun in 1603. His family ruled until 1868.

entries.title: Tōkyō
entries.description: Capital of Japan, formerly Edo. About 14 million people live in Tōkyō Prefecture.

entries.title: tomoe nagare
entries.description: Form of nagare: as kōhō tomoe nagare, swirling backward.

entries.title: tonki
entries.description: Throwing missiles. Another name for shuriken.

entries.title: tori no ko
entries.description: Firecrackers.

entries.title: torinawa
entries.description: Ninja weapon made of a rope with a weight and a spike, used to catch and tie up an opponent.

entries.title: tōtoku hyōshi no kamae
entries.description: Kneeling stance (kamae) of the Togakure-Ryū according to Bujinkan tradition: the rear knee on the ground, the front knee raised, sword or fists held protectively in front of the chest.

entries.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
entries.description: Daimyō of non-noble birth and a general in Oda Nobunaga’s service. After Oda’s death, he unified Japan. After Hideyoshi’s death, Tokugawa Ieyasu turned against his heirs, and his entire family was wiped out.

entries.title: tsuba
entries.description: Part of the sword that protected the hand from the opponent’s blows.

entries.title: tsubo giri
entries.description: Drill for larger holes in wooden walls and doors.

entries.title: tsugi bune
entries.description: Boat made of parts: according to tradition, each member of a ninja team carried one piece, and at the water they quickly put it together.

entries.title: tsuri bashigo
entries.description: Ladder that could be secured to a wall with additional hooks for safety.

entries.title: uchi
entries.description: Striking technique.

entries.title: uchi dake
entries.description: Bamboo container in which the ninja carried embers, so they could start a fire quickly.

entries.title: Uesugi Kenshin
entries.description: Daimyō who tried to seize power in Japan during the Sengoku period. According to tradition, he died in the privy: a ninja is said to have waited in the shaft and killed him.

entries.title: ukemi gata taihen jutsu
entries.translation: the art of rolling and falling

entries.title: uki daru
entries.description: Water tool made of two barrels, as ninja books describe it: one foot went into each, and the ninja moved across the water with a pole or a paddle. Also taru ikada.

entries.title: Ushiwakamaru
entries.description: Childhood name of Minamoto no Yoshitsune.

entries.title: uwagi
entries.description: Ninja jacket, tucked into the trousers, with hidden inside pockets.

entries.title: uzume bi
entries.description: Land mine. Also jirai.

entries.title: uzura gakure no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of hiding like a quail
entries.description: Technique of onshin jutsu: hiding in holes in the ground, hollows, and rock crevices, or behind stones.

entries.title: wakizashi
entries.description: Short sword of the samurai. Together with the katana, it formed the daishō.

entries.title: wakizashi teppō
entries.description: Traditional short sword with a hidden pistol that could fire one shot.

entries.title: wakō
entries.description: Japanese pirates who raided the coasts of Korea and China. Hardly any shōgun could match their strength. Many inventive ninja weapons are said to go back to the wakō.

entries.title: wari ashi
entries.description: Ninja walking technique.

entries.title: watari
entries.description: Ninja who sold their services to the highest bidder.

entries.title: wu wei
entries.description: Principle of Daoism: not acting against the natural course of the Dao.

entries.title: yaiba
entries.description: Upper part of the character nin (忍).

entries.title: yajiri
entries.description: Saw with a strong blade for thicker pieces of wood or branches.

entries.title: yamabiko jutsu
entries.description: Tōiri tactic: a ninja changed sides and served the new lord for years without raising doubts about their loyalty. At an agreed signal, the ninja switched back after causing great damage.

entries.title: yamabiko shichō no jutsu
entries.translation: the art of listening for the echo
entries.description: Chōhō technique: important documents were passed to a suspect, and their reaction was watched.

entries.title: yamabushi
entries.description: Hermits who lived secluded in the mountains and followed shugendō.

entries.title: yamidoko
entries.description: Flying device of the ninja. Also hito washi.

entries.title: yang
entries.description: The positive principle of the yin–yang duality in Daoism. In Japanese, yō.

entries.title: yarijutsu
entries.description: Spear techniques.

entries.title: yawara
entries.description: Fist weapon. Also kubotan.

entries.title: yin
entries.description: The negative principle of the yin–yang duality in Daoism. In Japanese, in.

entries.title: yinyang
entries.description: The duality of light and shadow, good and evil, small and large, an important principle of Daoism. In Japanese, in’yō.

entries.title: yoga
entries.translation: yoke, to yoke, to bind together, to harness
entries.description: Indian teaching of body and mind with many branches. In India, every <q>path to enlightenment</q> is a <q>yoga path</q>. Hatha yoga makes the body flexible enough to bend into extreme positions. Other forms also include diet, meditation, and breathing.

entries.title: yōji gakure no jutsu
entries.description: Heihō technique: the ninja kept throwing an object over a guard’s head until the guard stopped following up on every sound.

entries.title: yoko nagare
entries.description: Form of nagare: falling sideways from a standing position, to the right (migi yoko nagare) or to the left (hidari yoko nagare).

entries.title: yomogami no jutsu
entries.translation: a hairstyle must look the same from all four sides
entries.description: Chōhō principle: a ninja always kept several names and identities ready.

entries.title: yon shaku bō
entries.description: Staff four shaku long, about 121 centimeters. Also jō.

entries.title: yuki waraki
entries.description: Also geta.

entries.title: yumi
entries.description: Also kyū.

entries.title: zagarashijaku
entries.description: Fast-acting, deadly poison made from green plums or peaches.

entries.title: zazen
entries.description: Remaining in thought-free, wide-awake attention, with the mind directed at nothing. This practice goes back to the Buddha’s meditation before his awakening.

entries.title: ziran
entries.description: In Daoism, what happens of itself: spontaneously, from within, without force.
